title: Versailles pattern stone pavers
purpose: Generate tileable PBR maps of stone pavers in the Versailles (French) pattern: four sizes from an exact periodic module with no four-way joints and short straight joints, in tumbled travertine, walnut travertine, honed limestone or multicolour slate. Use for patios, terraces, pool decks and interior stone floors.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python versailles_pavers.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: repeats
parameters.meaning: Copies of the 13 x 13 unit pattern across the tile.

parameters.name: joint_width
parameters.meaning: Joint width in units (the side of the smallest square).

parameters.name: joint_fill
parameters.meaning: Height of the jointing sand or grout relative to the stone faces.

parameters.name: tumbling
parameters.meaning: Rounded, chipped and worn edges from tumbling: 0 crisp sawn edges.

parameters.name: pits
parameters.meaning: Travertine holes elongated along each piece's bedding.

parameters.name: veining
parameters.meaning: Banded colour along the bedding of each piece.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Tumbled ivory travertine in the Versailles pattern with sand joints.

presets.name: walnut_travertine
presets.description: Darker walnut and noce travertine, strongly banded and pitted.

presets.name: honed_limestone
presets.description: Honed limestone with crisp sawn edges, few pits and thin grout joints.

presets.name: multicolour_slate
presets.description: Gauged slate in grey, rust and green, two pattern repeats per tile.

limits: One fixed module: one piece each of 2 x 3, 2 x 2, 1 x 2 and 1 x 1 units repeated by a lattice of index 13, so the tile is 13 units square (or a multiple); other Versailles layouts and borders are out of scope. Travertine pits, bands, chips and slate colours are noise approximations, not measured stone. At small output sizes joints are thinner than a pixel. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate, not ray traced.
technique_references: Lattice tiling: a four-piece cluster as a complete residue system of the lattice (t, 4t mod 13)
Exhaustive search over cluster placements for no four-way joints and straight joints of at most four units
Rectangle side distances with tumbled, chipped edges
Anisotropic fractional Brownian motion for bedding bands and elongated pits
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
